newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank official sees new investment wave soon.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank official sees new investment wave soon.

text.p: The Czech Republic will soon experience another wave of direct foreign investment, this time into industry, central bank vice-governor Pavel Kysilka told a banking conference on Wednesday.
"We expect new investment wave soon, concentrated on enterprises," he said without elaborating.
Kysilka said the large investment flows into infrustructure and enviroment projects had already caused the trade and current account deficits to widen.

He reitereated statements made by central bank Governor Josef Tosovsky last week that the widening trade gap would push the current account into a deficit of six to seven percent this year after four percent in 1995.

"This development is understandable and natural," Kysilka told the conference. "(But thanks) to the country's foreign currency reserves and low debt service we see it (current account deficit) as sustainable in the medium term."
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has said that the Czech Republic would have a perpetual trade gap due to lack of natural resurces and structure of the economy.
The trade deficit reached 110.7 billion crowns in the first nine months of 1996, up from 62.3 billion in the same period last year.
The current accoount deficit stood at $1.7 billion in the first half of this year, up from $723 million in the first six months of 1995.
